articles.title: 1. Indus Valley Civilization (Harappan Culture)
articles.excerpt: Urban town planning, Great Bath, Harappa, Mohenjodaro, Lothal dockyard, script & key exam facts.
articles.body:
Overview & Chronology

Indus Valley Civilization (c. 2600–1900 BCE) was India's earliest bronze-age urban civilization across the Indus and Ghaggar-Hakra basins.

  • Town Planning: Grid system, burnt bricks, covered drainage, fortified citadel & lower town
  • Key Sites: Harappa (Ravi -- R-37 cemetery), Mohenjodaro (Indus -- Great Bath, dancing girl), Lothal (Bhogava -- dockyard), Kalibangan (ploughed field)
  • Trade & Economy: Pashupati seal, steatite seals, Mesopotamian trade links (Meluhha)
SiteRiver / LocationNotable Discovery
HarappaRavi (Montgomery)Granaries, coffin burial
MohenjodaroIndus (Larkana)Great Bath, bronze dancer
DholaviraRann of KutchWater reservoirs, sign board

articles.title: 2. Vedic Age: Early & Later Vedic Period
articles.excerpt: Rigvedic vs Later Vedic polity, sabha-samiti, four ashramas, varna system & sacred rivers.
articles.body:
Rigvedic vs Later Vedic Shift

Early Vedic (Rigvedic) society was pastoral and tribal, while Later Vedic age saw iron use, territorial kingdoms (Janapadas), and ritual complexity.

  • Rivers: Sindhu (most mentioned), Saraswati (most sacred), Ganga & Yamuna mentioned in Rigveda
  • Assemblies: Sabha, Samiti, Vidatha; king assisted by Purohita and Senani
  • Four Vedas: Rigveda (hymns), Samaveda (music), Yajurveda (sacrifices), Atharvaveda (charms & medicine)
AspectEarly VedicLater Vedic
Main OccupationCattle rearing & pastoralAgriculture & iron tools
PolityTribal Rajan, Sabha/SamitiTerritorial Janapadas, Bali tax
DeitiesIndra, Agni, VarunaPrajapati, Vishnu, Rudra

articles.title: 3. Rise of Second Urbanisation & 16 Mahajanapadas
articles.excerpt: Second urbanisation, NBPW pottery, punch-marked coins, 16 Mahajanapadas & Magadha ascendancy.
articles.body:
Second Urbanisation & Mahajanapadas

Around 6th century BCE, widespread iron technology, surplus farming, and coinage triggered Second Urbanisation and 16 Mahajanapadas listed in Anguttara Nikaya.

  • Southernmost Mahajanapada: Assaka / Ashmaka (Godavari region)
  • Republics (Gana-Sanghas): Vajji (Licchavis) and Malla
  • Magadha Rise: Haryanka, Shishunaga, and Nanda dynasties; strategic capitals Rajgir & Pataliputra
MahajanapadaCapitalKey Fact
MagadhaRajgir / PataliputraBimbisara, Ajatashatru, Mahapadma Nanda
AvantiUjjayini / MahishmatiPradyota dynasty
KosalaShravasti / AyodhyaPrasenajit

articles.title: 4. Buddhism: Life, Teachings & Councils
articles.excerpt: Gautama Buddha milestones, Four Noble Truths, Ashtangika Marga, Tripitakas & four councils.
articles.body:
Core Doctrines & Councils

Siddhartha Gautama (Buddha) preached middle path, Four Noble Truths (Arya Satyas), and Eightfold Path (Ashtangika Marga) in Pali.

  • Key Events: Birth (Lumbini), Enlightenment (Bodh Gaya under Bodhi tree), First Sermon (Sarnath -- Dharmachakra Pravartana), Mahaparinirvana (Kushinagar)
  • Tripitaka: Sutta Pitaka, Vinaya Pitaka, Abhidhamma Pitaka
  • Fourth Council: Under Kanishka in Kashmir -- split into Hinayana & Mahayana
CouncilVenue / PatronMain Outcome
1stRajagriha (Ajatashatru)Sutta & Vinaya compiled
2ndVaishali (Kalashoka)Sthaviravadins vs Mahasanghikas
3rdPataliputra (Ashoka)Abhidhamma Pitaka, Mogalliputta Tissa
4thKashmir (Kanishka)Hinayana & Mahayana division

articles.title: 5. Jainism: Tirthankaras, Triratna & Councils
articles.excerpt: Rishabhadeva, Mahavira, Panch Mahavrata, Triratna, Anekantavada & Shwetambara-Digambara.
articles.body:
Jain Philosophy & Sects

Vardhamana Mahavira was the 24th Tirthankara (1st: Rishabhadeva; 23rd: Parshvanatha), emphasizing Ahimsa, Syadvada, and Anekantavada.

  • Triratna: Right Faith (Samyak Darshana), Right Knowledge (Samyak Jnana), Right Conduct (Samyak Charitra)
  • Five Vows: Satya, Ahimsa, Asteya, Aparigraha (added by Parshvanatha) + Brahmacharya (added by Mahavira)
  • Sects: Shwetambara (white-clad, Sthulabhadra) & Digambara (sky-clad, Bhadrabahu)

articles.title: 6. Mauryan Empire: Administration & Ashoka's Dhamma
articles.excerpt: Chandragupta Maurya, Arthashastra, Megasthenes Indica, Ashokan edicts, Kalinga war & Dhamma.
articles.body:
Imperial Mauryan State

Founded by Chandragupta Maurya with Chanakya (Kautilya), the Mauryan Empire reached its zenith under Ashoka.

  • Sources: Kautilya's Arthashastra, Megasthenes' Indica, Mudrarakshasa, and Ashokan rock/pillar edicts
  • Kalinga War (261 BCE): Described in Major Rock Edict XIII; led to policy of Dhammaghosha
  • Officers: Dhamma Mahamattas (appointed by Ashoka), Rajukas, Pradeshikas, Samaharta (revenue)

articles.title: 7. Gupta Empire: Rulers, Art, Literature & Science
articles.excerpt: Samudragupta, Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya), Fahien, Navaratnas, Aryabhata, Kalidasa & temples.
articles.body:
Classical Gupta Era

Often termed a classical cultural peak in art, Sanskrit literature, and mathematics/astronomy.

  • Samudragupta: Napoleon of India (V.A. Smith), Prayag Prashasti by Harishena, Ashvamedha coins
  • Chandragupta II: Title Vikramaditya, silver coins, Fa-Hien's visit, Navaratnas (Kalidasa, Varahamihira, Amarasimha)
  • Science & Art: Aryabhata (zero, rotation of Earth, trigonometry), Dashavatara temple (Deogarh), Ajanta & Bagh murals

articles.title: 8. Chola Empire: Naval Power & Village Administration
articles.excerpt: Rajaraja I, Rajendra I, Gangaikonda Cholapuram, Brihadeeswarar temple, Nataraja bronze & Sabha.
articles.body:
Imperial Cholas of Thanjavur

Renowned for strong naval expeditions, Dravidian temple architecture, and autonomous village assemblies (Sabha & Ur).

  • Rajaraja I (985–1014 CE): Built Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur; naval strike on Sri Lanka & Srivijaya
  • Rajendra I: Expedition to Ganga, assumed title Gangaikondachola, built Gangaikonda Cholapuram
  • Local Governance: Uttaramerur inscriptions detail Kudavolai election system for village committees

articles.title: 9. Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526): Dynasties & Policies
articles.excerpt: Mamluk, Khilji, Tughlaq, Sayyid & Lodi dynasties, market control, Iqta system & administrative terms.
articles.body:
Five Sultanate Dynasties

Ruled from Delhi across five successive dynasties with distinct revenue and military systems.

  • Iltutmish: Organised Iqta system and Turkan-i-Chahalgani; silver Tanka and copper Jital
  • Alauddin Khilji: Market price control (Shahna-i-Mandi), Dagh (branding horses) & Huliya (descriptive roll)
  • Muhammad bin Tughlaq: Token currency experiment, transfer of capital to Daulatabad, Diwan-i-Kohi (agriculture)

articles.title: 10. Mughal Empire: Rulers, Mansabdari & Revenue
articles.excerpt: Babur, Humayun, Sher Shah, Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan, Aurangzeb, Mansabdari & Zabti/Dahsala.
articles.body:
Mughal Polity & Economy

Established after First Battle of Panipat (1526) by Babur, consolidated by Akbar and Sher Shah Suri.

  • Sher Shah Suri: Grand Trunk Road, Rupiya, Patta & Qabuliyat system
  • Akbar: Mansabdari (Zat & Sawar), Dahsala / Todar Mal bandobast, Din-i-Ilahi (1582), Ibadat Khana
  • Culture: Mughal miniature painting (peak under Jahangir), Taj Mahal & Red Fort (Shah Jahan)

articles.title: 11. Modern History: 1857 Revolt & Indian Freedom Movement (Page 2)
articles.excerpt: 1857 Uprising, INC 1885, Swadeshi, Non-Cooperation, Civil Disobedience, Quit India & 1947.
articles.body:
Freedom Movement Milestones (Page 2 Demo)

Ek page mein 10 articles ke baad yeh 11th article Page 2 / Next par open hota hai.

  • Revolt of 1857: Began at Meerut (10 May 1857); Rani Lakshmibai (Jhansi), Kunwar Singh (Bihar), Begum Hazrat Mahal (Lucknow)
  • Gandhian Era: Champaran (1917), Non-Cooperation (1920), Dandi March (1930), Quit India (1942 -- 'Do or Die')
  • Independence: Cabinet Mission (1946), Mountbatten Plan & Indian Independence Act (1947)
